children: By Emily Ou Yong
Iron ore futures rose on Friday, driven by a surge in freight costs and destocking at major ports in top buyer China, posting a second straight weekly gain.
The most-traded January iron ore contract on China's Dalian Commodity Exchange (DCE)
was 1.04% higher at 727 yuan ($108.25) a metric ton. The contract gained 0.62% this week.
The benchmark October iron ore (SZZFV6) on the Singapore Exchange was 0.26% higher at $99.4 a ton, rising 0.95% in the week.

The price surge was mainly driven by high freight costs stemming from bad weather in the Pacific, elevated oil prices and increased transhipment volumes from Guinea, a Malaysia-based market analyst said.

Freight costs on the Capesize C3 route from Brazil to Qingdao stood at $40.72 a ton on Thursday, up $1.11 from the day before, data from consultancy Mysteel showed. These are roughly double normal levels, the analyst said.
Oil prices rose on Friday, heading for their steepest weekly gain since mid-July, as rising tension and renewed U.S.-Iran hostilities heightened concerns over Middle East supply risks.
Iron ore inventory at major Chinese ports fell 1.38% week-on-week to 152.63 million tons, marking the fourth straight week of declines, data from consultancy Steelhome showed.
Brazilian miner Usiminas
temporarily suspended its Samambaia iron ore plant in Itatiaiuçu from September 2, citing weaker ore prices and sharply higher ocean freight costs, according to local media reports.
The suspension is expected to affect 170,000-200,000 tons of weekly shipments, supporting prices alongside the surge in freight costs, analysts from Chinese broker GF Futures said in a note.
Gains in ore prices were limited, however, by falling steel mill profitability, which was down 2.17 percentage points from a month earlier to 30.3% this week, Mysteel data showed.
Other steelmaking ingredients on the DCE rose, with coking coal
NYMEX:ACT1!
and coke (DCJcv1) up 0.66% and 0.6%, respectively.
Steel benchmarks on the Shanghai Futures Exchange were stronger. Rebar
rose 0.92%, hot-rolled coil
gained 0.54%, wire rod (SWRcv1) advanced 0.8% and stainless steel
edged 0.11% higher.
($1 = 6.7162 Chinese yuan)
